title: Awarapan 2 Opens to ₹12.86 Crore on Day 1 After Selling 2.85 Lakh Advance Tickets
excerpt: Emraan Hashmi's sequel to the 2007 cult classic recorded the third-highest pre-sales of 2026, outpacing Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947 by a wide margin on Independence Day weekend.
body:
• Awarapan 2 earned ₹12.86 crore at the domestic box office on its opening day, August 14, coinciding with India's Independence Day weekend.
  • The film sold approximately 2.85 lakh advance tickets across national chains, recording the third-highest pre-sales of 2026.
  • Emraan Hashmi's sequel outpaced rival release Batwara 1947 by roughly six times in ticket sales despite receiving only marginally more shows.
  • The film carries a U/A 16+ certificate and a 140-minute runtime, making it accessible to family audiences during the holiday weekend.

Emraan Hashmi's Awarapan 2 opened to ₹12.86 crore at the Indian box office on August 14, delivering the actor one of his strongest opening days in a career spanning over two decades. The romantic action thriller, directed by Nitin Kakkar and produced by Vishesh Bhatt under the Vishesh Films banner, arrived on India's Independence Day weekend to a massive advance booking wave.

Advance Booking Numbers

The film's advance booking campaign, which began on August 11, drew a strong response across PVR, INOX, and Cinepolis. By August 11 evening, Awarapan 2 had sold roughly 20,300 tickets in national chains alone, grossing approximately ₹86 lakh across more than 1,140 shows, according to Sacnilk. PVR led with about 10,000 tickets and ₹46 lakh in gross, followed by INOX at 6,500 tickets and Cinepolis at 3,800 tickets.

All-India advance booking figures showed the film grossing over ₹70 lakh from 21,160 tickets across nearly 2,700 tracked shows, with an average ticket price of ₹265. With blocked seats included, the potential gross reached ₹1.9 crore before opening day. On BookMyShow, the film crossed 298,000 interest likes, according to tracking data reported by Sacnilk.

"OGs know this isn't just a wrap. He came back for you. In cinemas August 14."

— Vishesh Films, via social media

Clash With Batwara 1947

Awarapan 2 opened against Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947, a Partition-era drama produced under the Aamir Khan production banner. The clash echoed the 2007 face-off when Deol's Apne defeated the original Awarapan at the box office. This time, the tables turned decisively.

According to Bollywood Hungama, Awarapan 2 sold six times more tickets than Batwara 1947 despite receiving only 282 more shows. In national chains, Batwara 1947 managed approximately 4,900 tickets for a total gross of about ₹20 lakh — a fraction of its competitor's figures. The sequel's U/A certification and shorter 140-minute runtime gave it an edge with family audiences compared to the A-rated period drama.

Box Office Trajectory

The film's day-one performance followed a strong build throughout the day. According to Bollywood Hungama, Awarapan 2 collected ₹3.5 crore by noon and jumped to ₹9.36 crore by 5 PM, ultimately finishing at ₹12.86 crore as reported by Wikipedia citing Bollywood Hungama. The opening positions it as potentially Emraan Hashmi's third-biggest opening day in India, behind Dhurandhar and its sequel.

Made on an estimated budget of ₹25–30 crore, according to Zoom TV, the film needs a first-week total in the range of ₹50–60 crore to be considered a clean hit. The Independence Day extended weekend and strong word of mouth could help it reach that target.

Critical Reception

Reviews have been mixed but lean positive. Hindustan Times gave it 3.5 out of 5 stars, describing it as an "intentionally old-school sequel" that recreates the atmosphere of 2000s Bollywood. Bollywood Hungama also awarded 3.5 stars, noting the film "falls short of the greatness of Awarapan [2007], which has become a cult classic." India Today gave 3 out of 5 stars, praising Hashmi's screen presence. The Indian Express rated it 2.5 stars, noting a strong first two acts let down by a "long, dull third act."

The sequel stars Disha Patani opposite Hashmi, with Shabana Azmi in a pivotal antagonist role and Suvinder Vicky as Jaideep. The soundtrack, composed by Mithoon, Amaal Mallik, Jeet Gannguli, and Akhil Sachdeva, includes a reimagined version of the iconic "Toh Phir Aao."

What's Next

With the Independence Day holiday weekend ahead, the film's trajectory over Saturday and Sunday will determine whether it can cross the ₹40 crore mark by Sunday night. Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which has already crossed ₹530 crore in India, continues to occupy premium evening slots, limiting screen availability for both new Bollywood releases.
